match.reason: No bank point covers this point's mix of limits: the closest, Pressures on future food supply, is about climate, water and urban spread reducing supply, while this point also needs the lack of good farmland left to clear and the competition from biofuel crops, which are not in any bank card.

draft.title: Limits on producing more food
card: Growing more food is not as simple as farming more land. Most of the world's good farmland is already in use. Clearing the land that is left, such as rainforest, destroys habitats and releases stored carbon.
Water is scarce in many farming regions. Crops, especially irrigated ones, need a lot of it, and rivers and underground water can be used up faster than rain refills them.
Land degradation means soil loses its quality, through erosion, salt build-up or loss of nutrients. Degraded land grows less food, so farmland can be lost even when it is not built on.
Farmland also faces competition. Growing cities spread over farmland, and biofuel crops, which are grown to make fuel, use land that could grow food.
draft.remember: More food cannot simply come from more farmland: land is limited, water is scarce, soil degrades and other uses compete.

a.q: Why can the world not feed a growing population just by clearing more land for farms?
opts: Most good farmland is already in use
Cleared land never grows any crops
Farmers prefer to use less land
Water is plentiful on all new land
a.why: Most of the best farmland is already farmed, so the land that remains is limited and clearing it brings costs such as lost habitat. Cleared land can grow crops, so saying it never does is wrong.
a.clue: Think about how much good farmland is still unused.

b.q: Near a city in Victoria, a farm's soil has become salty and now grows far less wheat than it once did. Which limit on food production does this show?
b.why: Salt build-up lowers soil quality, which is land degradation. The farm has not been built over or switched to fuel crops, so those options do not fit. The land is still there but grows less food.
b.clue: The farm is still farmland, but its soil has changed.

a.best: Most good farmland is already in use
